Corporate Finance

Lecture 6 extras: Spurious correlations, and a trader at La Défense

Camilo Saldarriaga

Finance Department, ESCP Business School, 2025/2026

A. Spurious correlations: data snooping in action

Remember data snooping?

  • If you test hundreds of characteristics on the same past data some will “beat the market” by pure luck. That is data snooping.

  • When evaluating statistical relations on several data sets, some patterns will apper by luck.

  • The website Spurious Correlations (tylervigen.com) does this on purpose: it keeps the pairs of series with a correlation close to 1. Reminder from Lecture 2: \[\text{Corr}(X,Y) = \frac{\text{Cov}(X,Y)}{\sigma_{X}\,\sigma_{Y}}\] The covariance rescaled by the two volatilities, so it lies between \(-1\) and \(+1\).

Search long enough and you will always find a pattern. Finding one proves nothing about the future.

Pork spending and Lululemon

  • Correlation 0.97.

Will Smith and electricity in Kosovo

  • Correlation of 0.85.

American cheese and BlackRock

  • Correlation of 0.94. Both series simply grow over time, so they look alike.

A high correlation raises a question. Only an economic reason can answer it.

B. L’Outsider: one trader, 50 billion euros

The Kerviel case in one slide

  • Jérôme Kerviel, a junior trader at Société Générale in La Défense. His job: small, low-risk bets on European stock indices.

  • In 2007 he secretly built up bets worth about EUR 50 billion, hidden with fake trades that cancelled them out on paper.

  • January 2008: the bank discovers the positions and sells them in a few days, in a falling market. The loss: EUR 4.9 billion.

  • 2010: he is sentenced to prison and ordered to repay the EUR 4.9 billion. 2016: an appeal court cuts that to EUR 1 million, because the bank’s own controls had failed.

50 billion is what was at risk. 4.9 billion is what was actually lost.

How big is EUR 50 billion?

  • More than the whole bank. In 2007, all of Société Générale’s shares together were worth EUR 43.16 billion (its market capitalization), less than the bets of this one trader.

  • More than the yearly output of whole countries. EUR 50 billion (about USD 54 billion) is more than everything produced in one year (GDP, 2024) in:

    • Estonia: about USD 43 billion
    • Cyprus: about USD 37 billion
    • Iceland: about USD 34 billion

The film and the documentary

  • L’Outsider (2016), by Christophe Barratier, with Arthur Dupont as Kerviel. Tagline: “You can cheat to win, not to lose.”

  • Kerviel: un trader, 50 milliards (Breaking the Bank: One Trader, 50 Billion, 2024): a four-part documentary on HBO Max, with Kerviel and his former bosses.
